headline: CoreWeave's shares and bonds headed for a steep weekly loss as investors worry the AI cloud company cannot carry its $50 billion of debt if interest rates rise.
score_reason: Reuters-confirmed worst week in 11 months for a leading AI infrastructure borrower, with record debt-insurance costs and spread to rivals.
importance_line: Holders of CoreWeave shares and bonds lose first, then lenders and rival AI cloud firms facing higher borrowing costs, but it is unclear whether CoreWeave is a special case, as Evercore analysts argue its business model has not stopped working.
summary: Reuters reports that CoreWeave, an Nvidia-backed company that rents out AI computing power, fell more than 11% on Friday, taking its loss for the week to nearly 25%, on course for its worst week in over 11 months, as worries grew over its $50 billion of debt. This continues our 15 Oct report on its slump; new is that the cost of insuring its debt passed 1,000 basis points, a record, and that rivals Nebius, Applied Digital and IREN fell 9% to 10% as well.
notes: Reuters text read on the Central Oregon Daily copy; reuters.com link kept as the original. Follow-up of the 15 Oct item on CoreWeave's 14 Oct fall.
